- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp price spikes — apply downward bias to later forecast days.  
- If true outcome shows strong upward trend after a dip, model often fails to capture the momentum — adjust forecast to reflect accelerating growth.  
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — overcorrects after sharp moves, leading to premature flattening — avoid this by preserving recent trend direction.  
- When sentiment is neutral or negative, model tends to forecast flat or downward — if true outcome rises, apply upward correction to avoid missing breakout.  
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging the true trend — especially after sentiment shifts — consider smoothing with 1-2 day lag correction.
